skin_texture.roughness_basis: Reconstructed engineering value, not measured from a period person or calibrated capture.
skin_texture.identity_basis: MakeHuman's own CC0 older light-skinned male system atlas, its painted scalp stubble blended to skin for a bald crown (tools/human_skin_bald_scalp.py); not a likeness or an attested complexion.
skin_texture.uv_status: hm08 base-mesh UV layout, as the toigo atlases; checked on the built figure.

hair_component.appearance_basis: Shared cleared CC0 short04 cap, kept as the skull surface the strand hair grows from; for a bald cut human-hair.js hides it at runtime. No hairstyle or likeness is asserted by the cap.

eye_components.source_basis: Actual helper centers/axes; original opaque sclera/iris/pupil, reconstructed dimensions and brown color, not resident facts

label: Reconstructed 1904 gentleman's day dress (frock coat, high waistcoat, standing collar and tie, grey trousers, black boots, black derby) on the shared portable male rig
basis: Original shirt, waistcoat and frock-coat shells offset from the cleared adult body's own surface, frock-coat skirts lofted round its sections, trousers on the shared workwear shell, a tie laid on the shirt, a derby seated round the skull and closed boots round the feet, cut after the day dress the reference pictures show (T-3441). Seams, ease, lengths and colours are reconstructed. Complete source anatomy remains unchanged beneath clothing.
source_scope: Glessner's own undated halftone portrait (printed 1910, captioned for his 1897 presidency of the Commercial Club) shows his collar, tie, waistcoat and coat at the shoulders; a 1904 Clinedinst studio print of Taft and Root (LOC, no known restrictions) shows the frock coat, waistcoat, collar and trousers of the year full length; an Underwood & Underwood stereograph of State Street, Chicago, at noon in 1903 (LOC) shows the derby and dark coats worn by day in the city. All are monochrome; no pixels or traced shapes enter the asset.

body_parameters.height_basis: The shared engineering body; the variation kit draws height and build at runtime. Not a recorded height.
body_parameters.age_basis: Engineering body at the kit base age 35; human-variation.js ages him to 61 from his record (born 1843).
body_parameters.shape_basis: CC0 male macro targets; equal software-category blend is engineering only, not inferred ancestry or a portrait.

proof_variants.body_basis: CC0 adult-male graphical body and an older light-skinned generic skin are reconstructed authoring choices. John J. Glessner is an attested person; his face is fitted to his photograph at runtime (hm08_variation_persons.json); no complexion, height or outfit of his is asserted.

gentleman_components.evidence_choice: The brief allowed a frock coat, a morning coat or a sack suit. The 1904 Taft and Root print shows two public men in frock coats; the 1903 State Street stereograph shows Chicago men by day mostly in sack coats and derbies, with a frock coat among them; Glessner's own plate shows a high waistcoat, a tall standing collar and a four-in-hand tie under a dark coat. A frock coat with a derby joins all three for a 61-year-old executive.

provenance.source_scope: Glessner's own plate shows a white shirt with a tall standing collar reaching nearly to the jaw; Root (1904) wears a tall wing collar. The collar's top falls 24 mm toward the throat so it stands on the neck and clears the chin, and the band stands 5 mm off the neck as a starched collar does (owner, 2026-11-07, T-3456, T-3470). Height, ease and the white are read from the monochrome pictures; the linen is reconstructed.
Glessner's plate shows a dark four-in-hand tie knotted at the collar; its width and silk are reconstructed.

A dark single-breasted waistcoat cut high on the chest, its opening a short narrow V showing little more than the collar and tie, as in Glessner's plate and on Root in 1904; its cloth matches the coat (a reconstructed choice).

Root and Taft (1904) and a man on State Street, Chicago (1903) wear dark single-breasted frock coats with rolled lapels and skirts to the knee. That Glessner wore one on a weekday in 1904 is not recorded: chosen as the formal day dress of an executive of 61 in these pictures. Black wool is reconstructed.
Straight trousers to the shoe with a small break, mid-grey, as Taft's (1904) and the State Street men's (1903) read; the grey is reconstructed (Taft's are striped, not modelled).
Black polished footwear under the trouser hem, as in the 1904 portrait; boots rather than shoes are a reconstructed choice (only the foot shows).
Nearly every man on State Street at noon in 1903 wears a black derby, the frock-coated man among them; its crown and brim are reconstructed.
